Summary: Browser's automatic GET /favicon.ico request after /login was clearing the anonymous login session, wiping the CSRF token before the user could submit the login form
Reproduction steps: 1. GET /login in a real browser (not the Flask test client). 2. Browser automatically requests /favicon.ico. 3. before_request's session.clear() fired for that unauthenticated request too, invalidating the CSRF token the login form had just been issued.
M4 disposition: Fixed implementation has passing automated regression evidence; independent final-branch review pending.

Summary: Two test functions in tests/test_request_submission.py both named test_missing_csrf_does_not_write - Python silently kept only the second definition, so the original CSRF-rejection test never actually ran despite the suite reporting all green
Reproduction steps: 1. grep -c '^def test_' tests/test_request_submission.py vs pytest --collect-only -q - count mismatch (11 defs, 10 collected).
Regression evidence: Second definition renamed to test_service_rejects_staff_request_creation (TST-015); original CSRF test now collects under its own name (TST-013)
M4 disposition: Fixed implementation has passing automated regression evidence; independent final-branch review pending.

Summary: src/persistence/outbox.py::OutboxProcessor.process_pending catches a blind `except Exception`, which would silently swallow an unexpected error (e.g. a programming mistake) alongside the delivery failures it's meant to catch
Reproduction steps: ruff check src/ tests/ wsgi.py - BLE001 at src/persistence/outbox.py:23.
Regression evidence: No regression test yet - owned by Don (src/persistence/ is his file); reported, not fixed here, per M3 ownership boundaries.
Linked requirement/test: NFR-006 (auditability - a swallowed bug here could hide a real failure), ADR-004
M4 disposition: Retained: catch logs exceptions, but broad delivery/programming-error classification remains a concern; not silently closed.
